label: D37-sinkron-status-kartu
decision: How should the Anastrophe iOS app learn the server-side status of its cards (ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, REVOKED) after an operator suspends, resumes or revokes them (FR-38, ADR-0036), given that push notifications are not available yet?

candidates.description: When a credential is provisioned (and on renewal if missing), the server issues a random 32-byte status token per card instance, stores only its SHA-256, and the app keeps it in the Keychain with afterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly. On foreground (throttled, online only) the app calls GET /v1/cards/{id}/status with the token as a bearer credential and updates the local card status; 410 CARD-GONE marks the card revoked. No key signature, so no prompt.

Add POST /v1/credentials/{cred}:status using a :challenge nonce and a credential-key signature over 'ANP1-STATUS' ‖ cred_id ‖ nonce. The app runs it only inside actions the user already authenticated (presentation or renewal), so there is no extra prompt, but status updates only when the card is used.

Add card_status (ACTIVE or SUSPENDED) to the existing unauthenticated :challenge 201 response. The app polls :challenge on foreground (throttled) and updates the local status. One request, no new secret, but anyone who knows a cred_id can then distinguish SUSPENDED from ACTIVE.
No new call: :renew's 409 gains a reason (suspended or channel_blocked) and the app updates the status only when it renews (after a tap or near expiry); 410 CARD-GONE marks the card revoked.

priorities: 1) Security and privacy: nobody who only knows a cred_id or device_id learns more than today, and no secret is stored raw on the server. 2) Usability on a real iPhone: no Face ID or passcode prompt outside an action the user started. 3) Timeliness: the app reflects a suspension or resumption soon after it happens while online. 4) Minimal new API surface and reuse of existing patterns.
requirements: A party that knows only a cred_id or a device_id cannot learn whether a card is suspended.
On a real iPhone, refreshing the status never triggers a Face ID or passcode prompt outside an action the user started.
While online, the app reflects a suspension or resumption at its next foreground refresh, without a tap or a renewal.
